description: Van Woustraat 54-72 (1886-87): 5.7-6.1 m fronts of a shop and three tall upper storeys of dark brown brick; three axes of white T-windows under segmental brick heads; white sills; a plain brick frieze to a thin cornice at 15.1 m; a short slate mansard with roof lights and one stone pediment dormer with a hoist beam over the middle axis

match.note: Van Woustraat 54-72 (1886-87); cornice 15.1 m on the 2023-01-03 strip at a 2.44 m camera height (3DBAG eaves 13.7-16.2 m); the 2023-01-03 skyline reads the tram wires or the mansard top (16.3-21 m), so the measured wall (#4f-#57 warm grey-brown on this overcast strip) is a criterion too and every placed pand is drawn at the 15.1 m line

pediment-dormer.note: 56-70: one stone pediment dormer over the middle axis, 15.3-17.2 m, with a hoist beam, standing on the slate roof behind the 15.1 m cornice (the photo's short mansard face with roof lights is drawn as the pitched roof)

door-left.note: a residential door at the left party wall beside the shop

rhythm.roofline: plain brick frieze, thin cornice at 15.1 m, slate mansard with one stone pediment dormer and a hoist beam
schemaLimits: the short slate mansard face (15.1-16.3 m) and its roof lights beside the dormer are drawn as the pitched roof: the kit's mansard put the dormer frames through the roof face and its slate coplanar with the party walls (audit)
the dormer's carved ears and side cheeks are plain

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2023-01-03 (camera height 2.44 m) pands 3-4 (68, 66) at 1.3x with a metre grid: shop to 4.4 m; storey-1 windows 4.6-6.9 m, storey-2 7.9-10.2 m, storey-3 11.3-13.6 m under segmental heads; brick frieze 14.0-14.8, cornice 15.1 m; mansard to 16.3 m; dormer 15.3-17.2 m; windows 1.1 m on 5.7 m
